title: Fund exclusions from the Investment Company Act: Sections 3(c)(1), 3(c)(5)(C) and 3(c)(7)
rule: An issuer is an investment company if it is primarily in the business of investing in securities, or invests in securities and holds investment securities worth over 40% of its non-cash, non-government assets, unless excluded: 3(c)(1), at most 100 beneficial owners; 3(c)(7), only qualified purchasers, such as individuals with $5,000,000 in investments; 3(c)(5)(C), issuers of no redeemable securities primarily acquiring mortgages, other liens on and interests in real estate. The first two bar public offerings; a Rule 506 offering is not public merely through general solicitation.
changeWatch: Amendments to Section 3(a) or 3(c) of the Investment Company Act or to the qualified purchaser definition.
